title: Decisions taken by the Governing Council of the ECB (in addition to decisions setting interest rates)
body:
Decisions taken by the Governing Council of the ECB (in addition to decisions setting interest rates) Skip to: Skip to navigation Skip to content Skip to footer EN Български Čeština Dansk Deutsch Eλληνικά English Español Eesti keel Suomi Français Gaeilge Hrvatski Magyar Italiano Lietuvių Latviešu Malti Nederlands Polski Português Română Slovenčina Slovenščina Svenska Menu Search Menu ANYTIME PAST MONTH PAST YEAR Search Options Image Preview Sort by ANYTIME PAST MONTH PAST YEAR Suggestions Home Media Explainers Research & Publications Statistics Monetary Policy The €uro Payments & Markets Careers Suggestions Sort by Relevance Date Decisions taken by the Governing Council of the ECB (in addition to decisions setting interest rates) November 2026 27 November 2026 External communication Agreement for Sweden to join T2 On 25 November 2026 the ECB announced that it had concluded an agreement with Sveriges Riksbank for Sweden to join T2, the Eurosystem’s real-time gross settlement system. More information is available in the press release issued at the occasion of the signing ceremony with ECB President Christine Lagarde and Sveriges Riksbank Governor Erik Thedéen of the T2 currency participation agreement. Market operations and market infrastructure and payments Acceptance of marketable assets issued on distributed ledger technology (DLT) platforms licensed under the EU DLT Pilot Regime as Eurosystem collateral On 19 November 2026 the Governing Council approved the acceptance of marketable assets issued on DLT platforms licensed under the EU DLT Pilot Regime Regulation (EU) 2022/858 and reachable via TARGET2-Securities (T2S) as eligible collateral for Eurosystem credit operations, subject to specific Eurosystem requirements. This decision is part of a roadmap exploring ways to expand eligibility to assets issued and settled entirely on DLT networks. The decision is due to take effect in June 2027 and is explained in a press release available on the ECB’s website. It follows the ECB announcement of 27 January 2026 that marketable assets issued in central securities depositories using DLT will be accepted as collateral. These decisions testify to the Eurosystem’s commitment to aligning its collateral framework with advances in technology, while upholding the principles of adequacy of collateral, safety, efficiency and a level-playing field. Macroprudential policy and financial stability Financial Stability Review – November 2026 On 12 November 2026 the Governing Council held an exchange of views on the basis of the November 2026 edition of the Financial Stability Review and authorised its publication on the ECB’s website. In addition to providing an overview of key financial stability vulnerabilities in the euro area, this edition includes three special features. The first discusses the financial stability implications of AI adoption in the real economy and the financial industry. The second explores the complex interplay between AI and cybersecurity. The third assesses the financial stability implications of large initial public offerings and equity issuance in general, as well as how they both interact with the trend towards passive investing. The Financial Stability Review was published on 18 November 2026 on the ECB’s website, together with a related press release . Banknotes and coins 2026 study on payment attitudes of consumers in the euro area On 12 November 2026 the Governing Council took note of the results of the 2026 study on the payment attitudes of consumers in the euro area and approved its publication on the ECB’s website. The results show that consumers are increasingly using digital means of payment, while cash continues to play an important role. Moreover, while payment practices are changing, consumers’ own preferences nonetheless remain stable. The results of the study , together with a related press release , are available on the ECB’s website. Advice on legislation ECB Opinion on the supervisory independence of the Bank of Greece and prevention of conflicts of interest of its members of staff and governance body On 4 November 2026 the Governing Council adopted Opinion CON/2026/33 at the request of the Greek Ministry of Economy and Finance. ECB Opinion on designating the Deutsche Bundesbank as a recipient of administrative data for statistical purposes On 10 November 2026 the Governing Council adopted Opinion CON/2026/34 at the request of the Deutsche Bundesbank on behalf of the German Federal Ministry for Economic Affairs and Energy. ECB Opinion on the competences of the Supervisory Board of the Magyar Nemzeti Bank On 19 November 2026 the Governing Council adopted Opinion CON/2026/35 at the request of the Hungarian Ministry of Finance. ECB Opinion on a tax on excess profits of credit institutions and other specified companies On 25 November 2026 the Governing Council adopted Opinion CON/2026/36 at the request of the Bulgarian Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance. Corporate governance ECB Recommendation on the external auditors of the Bank of Greece On 5 November 2026 the Governing Council adopted Recommendation ECB/2026/29 to the Council of the European Union on the external auditors of the Bank of Greece. International and European cooperation Eurosystem participation in Phase II of Project Agorá On 18 November 2026 the Governing Council approved the participation of the Eurosystem – represented by the Banque de France – in Phase II of the BIS Innovation Hub’s Project Agorá which is due to run until December 2027. This ongoing Eurosystem participation in Agorá is without prejudice to any future policy decisions the Eurosystem may take on the possibility of providing central bank money on external or shared DLT platforms. At the invitation of the Banque de France and the ECB, other interested Eurosystem national central banks may join a newly established Eurosystem technical group to operationalise this participation in Project Agorá Phase II. ECB Banking Supervision Disclosure of Supervisory Review and Evaluation Process (SREP) methodologies On 3 November 2026 the Governing Council did not object to a proposal by the Supervisory Board to publish: the SREP 2026 methodology applied to significant institutions under the direct supervision of the ECB, the more detailed SREP methodology for operational risk and ICT risk, the more detailed SREP methodology for assessing capital adequacy, and the internal governance and risk management SREP methodology. The related press release, together with these four documents, is available on the ECB’s banking supervision website. Results of the SREP 2026 exercise On 9 November 2026 the Governing Council did not object to a proposal by the Supervisory Board to publish the SREP 2026 aggregated results. Overall, these results show that the euro area banking sector has continued to be resilient in the face of the heightened uncertainty clouding the economic and geopolitical environment. The publication is available on the ECB’s banking supervision website. Outcome of the 2026 risks and priorities exercise On 12 November 2026 the Governing Council did not object to a proposal by the Supervisory Board to publish the outcome of the 2026 risks and priorities exercise, listing the supervisory priorities for the next three years (2027-29). The publication is available on the ECB’s banking supervision website. 2027 Supervisory Examination Programme (SEP) for on-site inspections and internal model investigations at significant institutions On 16 November 2026 the Governing Council did not object to a proposal by the Supervisory Board concerning the 2027 SEP for on-site inspections and internal model investigations at significant institutions under European banking supervision. The on-site SEP is based on the SSM supervisory priorities for 2027-29 published on the ECB’s banking supervision website. Less significant institution (LSI) supervision report 2026 On 23 November 2026 the Governing Council did not object to a proposal by the Supervisory Board to publish a report on the supervision of LSIs in 2026. The report , which examines the structural features of the LSI sector, its key developments and major supervisory activities, is available on the ECB’s banking supervision website. title: ECB Consumer Expectations Survey results – October 2026
body:
ECB Consumer Expectations Survey results – October 2026 Skip to: Skip to navigation Skip to content Skip to footer EN Български Čeština Dansk Deutsch Eλληνικά English Español Eesti keel Suomi Français Gaeilge Hrvatski Magyar Italiano Lietuvių Latviešu Malti Nederlands Polski Português Română Slovenčina Slovenščina Svenska Menu Search Menu ANYTIME PAST MONTH PAST YEAR Search Options Image Preview Sort by ANYTIME PAST MONTH PAST YEAR Suggestions Home Media Explainers Research & Publications Statistics Monetary Policy The €uro Payments & Markets Careers Suggestions Sort by Relevance Date PRESS RELEASE ECB Consumer Expectations Survey results – October 2026 27 November 2026 Compared with September 2026: median consumer perceptions of inflation over the past 12 months and expectations for inflation over the next 12 months increased significantly, while median expectations for inflation three years ahead increased slightly and those for five years ahead were unchanged; expectations for nominal income growth over the next 12 months declined, while expectations for spending growth over the next 12 months were unchanged; expectations for economic growth over the next 12 months increased, while the expected unemployment rate in 12 months’ time decreased; expectations for growth in the price of homes over the next 12 months decreased, while expectations for mortgage interest rates in 12 months’ time remained unchanged. Inflation In October the median rate of perceived inflation over the previous 12 months increased to 4.1% from 3.6% in September and stood at its highest level since July 2024. Median expectations for inflation over the next 12 months also rose to 3.5% from 3.1%, but remained below the level reached at the start of the conflict in March 2026 (4.0%). Median expectations for inflation three years ahead increased to 3.0% from 2.9%, returning to the March 2026 level. Median expectations for inflation five years ahead were unchanged at 2.5% for the third consecutive month, the highest level since the start of the series in August 2022. Uncertainty about expectations for inflation over the next 12 months increased for the second consecutive month, remaining higher than the level prior to the start of the conflict in the Middle East. Respondents in the bottom income quintile continued to report higher inflation perceptions and expectations, on average, than those in the top quintile. Younger respondents (aged 18-34) continued to report lower inflation perceptions and expectations than older respondents (aged 35-54 and 55-70). Inflation results Income and consumption Consumers’ expectations for nominal income growth over the next 12 months fell to 0.6% from 1.1% in September. While expectations declined across all income quintiles, the decline was most pronounced in the bottom income quintile (by 0.7 percentage points to 0.8%) and in the top quintile (by 0.8 percentage points to 0.4%). Perceived nominal spending growth over the previous 12 months increased to 5.4% from 5.3% in September, while expected nominal spending growth over the next 12 months was unchanged at 3.7%. Income and consumption results Economic growth and labour market Expectations for economic growth over the next 12 months increased in October to -1.3% from -1.5% in September. Expectations for the unemployment rate 12 months ahead decreased to 11.0% from 11.3% in September. As observed in previous months, households in the bottom income quintile expected the highest unemployment rate 12 months ahead (13.3%), while households in the top income quintile expected the lowest rate (9.5%). Consumers continued to expect the future unemployment rate to be only slightly higher than the perceived current unemployment rate (10.4%), suggesting a broadly stable labour market outlook. Quarterly data revealed a somewhat mixed labour market sentiment. Unemployed respondents reported a lower expected probability of finding a job over the next three months, at 29.6% in October compared with 30.8% in July. Employed respondents reported a lower expected probability of job loss over the next three months, at 9.4% in October compared with 9.8% in July. Economic growth and labour market results Housing and credit access Consumers expected the price of their home to increase by 3.3% over the next 12 months, lower than in September (3.5%). As in previous months expectations for home price growth over the next 12 months remained, on average, higher in the lowest income quintile (3.8%) than in the highest income quintile (3.0%). Expectations for mortgage interest rates in 12 months’ time remained unchanged from July, at 4.9%. As in previous months, households in the top income quintile expected the lowest mortgage interest rates 12 months ahead (4.6%), while those in the bottom quintile expected the highest rates (5.4%). The net percentage of households reporting a tightening (relative to those reporting an easing) of access to credit over the previous 12 months increased compared with September. The net percentage of households expecting tighter credit conditions over the next 12 months (relative to those expecting an easing) also increased compared with September, reaching its highest value since October 2023. Quarterly data showed that the share of consumers who reported having applied for credit during the past three months increased slightly to 14.4% in October, from 14.3% in July. Housing and credit access results The release of the Consumer Expectations Survey (CES) results for November is scheduled for 7 January 2027. For media queries, please contact: Benoit Deeg , tel.: +49 172 1683704. Notes The fieldwork for the latest CES wave was carried out between 1 October and 2 November 2026. The main aggregate results for individual countries and the euro area are published on the ECB Data Portal and on the ECB’s website every month. Unless otherwise indicated, the statistics presented in this press release refer to the 2% winsorised mean. For further details, see ECB Consumer Expectations Survey – Guide to the computation of aggregate statistics . The CES is a monthly online survey of, currently, around 19,000 adult consumers (i.e. aged 18 or over) from 11 euro area countries: Belgium, Germany, Ireland, Greece, Spain, France, Italy, the Netherlands, Austria, Portugal and Finland. The results are used for policy analysis and complement other data sources used by the ECB. Further information about the survey and the data collected is available on the CES web page . Detailed information can also be found in the following two publications: Bańkowska, K. et al., “ ECB Consumer Expectations Survey: an overview and first evaluation ”, Occasional Paper Series , No 287, ECB, Frankfurt am Main, December 2021; and Georgarakos, D. and Kenny, G., “ Household spending and fiscal support during the COVID-19 pandemic: Insights from a new consumer survey ”, Journal of Monetary Economics , Vol. 129, Supplement, July 2022, pp. S1-S14. The survey results do not represent the views of the ECB’s decision-making bodies or staff. title: 15 years of investing in Colombia’s talent and future
body: 15 years of investing in Colombia’s talent and future Nov 26, 2026 | x.com Facebook LinkedIn Mail Copy link Google celebrates 15 years in Colombia with $1 million  in Google.org funding for AI education, small businesses, rural youth, and disaster relief. Edgardo Frias Country Director, Andean Region Share x.com Facebook LinkedIn Mail Copy link Your browser does not support the audio element. Listen to article [[duration]] minutes This content is generated by Google AI. Generative AI is experimental Voice Speed Voice Speed 0.75X 1X 1.5X 2X Fifteen years ago, Google’s story in Colombia began with five people and a clear belief: technology is most meaningful when it serves people’s ideas, projects, and dreams. Since opening our local office and launching YouTube in Colombia in 2011, we’ve grown together. Over the years, we’ve shared the journey with Colombians from their first search query to their latest prompt. We’ve introduced tools for everyday life and safety — like Android Earthquake Alerts , Google Wallet, Gemini, YouTube Kids and Family Link — and helped showcase local culture through Google Street View imagery across more than 51 cities and landmarks like the Coffee Cultural Landscape. 15 years of building together Today, Colombia’s curiosity and talent continue to inspire us. You can see it in creators like Profe Alex , who started in a classroom in Duitama and now teaches math on YouTube to over 10 million subscribers. You can also see it in young builders like Elvis Better in Soledad and Juan José Tabares in Tuluá — graduates of Impacto Maker , a program supported by Google.org , that trained 75,000 students and teachers in generative AI. Using Gemini, Elvis created mobile STEAM classrooms for local neighborhoods, and Juan José built a device for people with motor disabilities. Investing in Colombia’s future talent AI has the potential to spark new ideas and opportunities — and according to the AI Sprinters report , strong AI adoption could add between $7.2 billion and $13.6 billion annually to Colombia’s economy. Reaching that potential requires investing in people. Since 2019, Grow with Google has helped more than 13,500 Colombians graduate, including military veteran Jaime Olivera in Neiva, who trained in cybersecurity and now advises three companies as an ethical hacker. To build on this momentum for our 15th anniversary, we’re announcing more than $1 million in Google.org funding across four areas: Humanitarian relief: Supporting the Center for Disaster Philanthropy to help rebuild communities affected by last August’s earthquake. AI education: Bringing Experience AI — from the Raspberry Pi Foundation and Google DeepMind — to Colombia with Fundación Pies Descalzos to train 1,600 teachers and reach 40,000 students in Atlántico and Bolívar. Small business support: Backing an AI literacy program led by CENIA and Fundación Futuro del Trabajo to train nearly 15,000 Colombian small businesses. Rural youth opportunities: Supporting Colnodo’s JuvenTIC program to train 300 rural youth, prioritizing women, ethnic communities, armed conflict survivors and people with disabilities. We’re proud to share our tools and research, but the vision and next big idea will always come from you. Thank you for 15 years of building together. Accept recommended cookies Proceed with necessary cookies only Skip to main content Payments systems Memorandum of Understanding Bank of England, PRA, FCA and PSR review Memorandum of Understanding in relation to payment systems in the UK Published on  
        26 November 2026 Authorities complete 2026 review of Payments Memorandum of Understanding The Bank of England (the Bank), Financial Conduct Authority (FCA), Prudential Regulation Authority (PRA) and Payment Systems Regulator (PSR) have completed their annual review of the Memorandum of Understanding (MoU) on payments. The Authorities have considered the effectiveness and efficiency of their coordination under the MoU. This includes feedback from industry and regulated firms to determine whether the MoU’s principles of coordination and cooperation continue to be met in practice. The review found that cooperation and coordination remain effective, with respondents welcoming tangible progress in how the Authorities work together. Examples of this include collaborating on a range of developments, including the future regime for dual regulated stablecoin issuers and other innovations in payments, including the work of the Payments Vision Delivery Committee. Following the review, the Authorities have concluded that no changes to the MoU are needed at this time. The Authorities have provided further updates to the information detailing each Authority’s regulatory remit and will continue working together to identify areas where greater coordination would benefit the industry. This will help firms navigate the regulatory landscape and support a more coordinated and effective approach to payments regulation. This approach is further embedded through the Government’s decision to consolidate the PSR into the FCA, meaning greater coordination, clearer responsibilities and a simpler experience for firms. title: Come for the Games, Stay for the Community With GeForce NOW
body: Come for the Games, Stay for the Community With GeForce NOW Save 30% with the Black Friday membership sale, claim a ‘War Thunder’ reward and explore 12 new games this week. November 26, 2026 by GeForce NOW Community 0 Comments Share Share This Article X Facebook LinkedIn Copy link Link copied! Good games bring people together. This GFN Thursday, GeForce NOW is celebrating the members, creators and community moderators who turn every session into something worth sharing. From friendships formed in online lobbies to new worlds explored on everyday devices, GeForce NOW Ambassadors share their reasons to love cloud gaming. Those ready to find their own can get 30% off six-month Performance and Ultimate memberships in the Black Friday sale and a special seasonal offer through Amazon Fire TV Sticks. Plus, War Thunder gets a new look with NVIDIA DLSS 5 for Ultimate members and a Ready for Battle Pack reward is now available across all membership tiers. Rounding out the week, 12 new games join the GeForce NOW library . The Gamers Behind the Cloud Behind every screenshot, helpful tip and play session is a gamer with a story. GeForce NOW Ambassadors share what keeps them playing. For Discord moderator Luna, a low-spec laptop was the start of lasting connections: “Without GFN, I might’ve not been able to meet certain close friends … It has extended to me being given the privilege to be a moderator of an ever-growing community that links people together and continues to allow friends or partners to play with each other, regardless of what they own at home.” After years helping moderate the community’s Reddit and Discord spaces, Hamza went from an aging laptop to cloud gaming across a TV, phone, tablet and desktop: “ I’m genuinely thankful not just for the technology that keeps me gaming effortlessly wherever I am, but for the amazing community and friendships I’ve built along the way, and I look forward to what the future holds for cloud gaming.” GeForce NOW kept new releases within reach for moderator Flacz , without needing frequent hardware upgrades: “GeForce NOW allowed me to enjoy games and adventures I’ve never imagined to be possible and it continues to be a part of my daily gaming experience till this day.” The cloud brings the games. The community brings them to life. “Cyberpunk 2077” photo by Flacz. For creators such as Warwick , playing is only part of the picture: “GFN has allowed me to play the games I want, as soon as they come out. The support GFN has given me to create content for them and be partnered with them means the world and encourages me to get better each day.” Freedom to play and create resonates with Nads : “Being able to jump into my favorite games in an instant without worrying about downloads, storage limits or constant hardware upgrades feels like magic … Being able to play my game and stream on YouTube at the same time is something I never could have imagined before.” Nigiri21Sushi also turns to the cloud when games stretch a local PC: “As a gaming content-creator, my current PC sometimes struggles showcasing new-release games that are CPU/GPU-intensive … Hence, huge thank you to GFN for allowing me to produce fluid content via cloud-gaming.” For Marchief , demanding games on Steam Deck are the draw: “I’m thankful that GeForce NOW allows me to play the top AAA games on the Steam Deck … Having the power of an RTX 5080 in a handheld is just absolutely mindblowing.” Markys enjoys the comfort of the couch with his favorite game, World of Warcraft: Forever : “No high-end gaming PC needed, just my controller, my TV and the freedom to play wherever I want.” Anytime Anywhere Gaming shared a video that shared why GeForce NOW is  “ really fantastic in a whole lot of ways. ” Keep the conversation going on the community-run GeForce NOW Reddit and Discord . More Play, Less to Pay A little less spending. A lot more playing. There’s still time to save 30% on the first six-month term of a Performance or Ultimate membership . The Black Friday sale runs through Monday, Nov. 30, for new memberships and eligible upgrades in select regions, while supplies last. Go Ultimate for GeForce RTX 5080-class performance across PCs, Macs, Steam Deck and other supported handhelds, mobile devices, compatible TVs and more . Experience DLSS 5 in supported games, ray tracing and streaming at up to 5K resolution or up to 360 frames per second, with sessions lasting up to eight hours. GeForce NOW handles downloads, patches and updates for Ready-to-Play games, saving local storage for everyday essentials. Choose a six-month membership before the sale wraps up and settle in for a season of gaming. For big-screen play, GeForce NOW also supports Amazon Fire TV Stick devices, with a separate offer for 90% off the first month of Performance or Ultimate when purchased directly through Amazon in participating regions. Check out the supported devices and offer details . Ready for Battle, Rewarded in the Cloud A new look. A battle-ready bonus. Gaijin Entertainment’s War Thunder now supports NVIDIA DLSS 5 on GeForce NOW, bringing air, land and naval combat into sharper focus. Its 3D-Guided Neural Rendering technology adds lifelike lighting and materials, from tank armor to the water around a warship. Ultimate members can experience the visual update with GeForce RTX 5080-class performance in the cloud across supported devices, without an expensive PC upgrade. Keep the focus on the next maneuver and let GeForce NOW handle the power in the cloud. To celebrate, GeForce NOW members across all membership tiers can claim the Ready for Battle Pack, now available. The pack includes an M3A1 Stuart tank and F2A-1 aircraft, each with a unique skin, seven days of Premium account time, 100,000 Silver Lions, a 50% booster for Research Points and Silver Lions, and the “Overclocked” title. Sign in to a GeForce NOW account and head to the Account Portal to claim the reward code, then activate it on Gaijin’s redemption page . The reward is available through Friday, Dec. 25, at 11:59 p.m. PT, or while supplies last, with a limit of one per customer. Keep the great gaming going with this week’s additions to the GeForce NOW library: Sniper Ghost Warrior Contracts 2 ( Xbox , available on Game Pass Nov. 24) Arctic Drive (New release on Steam , Nov. 25) Appulse (New release on Steam , Nov. 26) GONE Fishing ( Steam ) Incursion Red River ( Steam ) John Carpenter’s Toxic Commando ( Xbox , available on Game Pass) Quasimorph ( Steam ) Ski-E-O! Ski Resort Tycoon ( Steam ) The Spell Brigade ( Steam ) World of Tanks: Blitz ( Wargaming.net ) Village in the Shade ( Steam ) Zombies Aren’t Real ( Steam ) Plus, Ultimate Members streaming from RTX 5080 cloud gaming rigs can experience Where Winds Mee t with DLSS 5 , enhancing the environments and characters of its wuxia open-world action role-playing game. Dates listed above reflect when games are released on their respective stores. GeForce NOW availability may vary, as games are onboarded after release and added throughout the week. Keep an eye on GeForce NOW channels and GFN Thursdays for availability updates on announced titles. Experience the best in GeForce NOW cloud gaming. Grab a day pass to try Performance or Ultimate before committing to a monthly membership, with the day pass cost applicable toward that first month. What’s the best part of gaming with GeForce NOW? Share it on X or in the comments below. title: Statistical Notice 2026/09 - Update to the classification of accounts guide
body:
Statistical Notice 2026/09 - Update to the classification of accounts guide | Bank of England – the UK's central bank Our use of cookies We use necessary cookies to make our site work. We’d also like to use some non-essential cookies (including third-party cookies) to help us improve the site. By clicking ‘Accept recommended settings’ on this banner, you accept our use of analytics cookies.   For more information on how these cookies work please see our Cookie policy . Accept recommended cookies Proceed with necessary cookies only Skip to main content Statistical Notice 2026/09 - Update to the classification of accounts guide Statistical Notices update the definitions and guidance contained in the Banking Statistics Yellow Folder Published on  
        26 November 2026 Statistical Notice 2026/09 Background The Bank of England has updated the Classification of Accounts Guide (CAG) to provide additional clarity on the classification of non-resident counterparties for statistical reporting purposes. The changes bring together guidance that is currently set out across the CAG and the Form CC/CL frequently asked questions. They are intended to improve the clarity and consistency of the published guidance and do not introduce new statistical reporting requirements. Changes to the Classification of Accounts Guide The Bank has updated its CAG on the following: Look-through approach for non-resident counterparties: as previously detailed in the Form CC/CL FAQs, the CAG has been clarified to explain that the look-through approach does not apply to non-resident counterparties in the same way as it applies to UK-resident counterparties. EU non-resident Deposit-taking Corporations: the guidance on the use of the European Central Bank’s published list has been clarified. An entity identified as a credit union on that list should be classified as a non-resident deposit-taking corporation. Sovereign wealth funds: sovereign wealth funds have been added to the examples of counterparties that should be classified as non-resident other financial corporations. Minor housekeeping changes: Minor changes have been made to improve the readability of the CAG. Reporting Implications These amendments clarify the Bank’s existing statistical reporting guidance. They do not introduce new data requirements or changes to reporting forms. Reporting institutions should review the updated CAG, and ensure that the clarified guidance is reflected in their own classification of counterparties when completing relevant statistical returns. The updated guide applies from 26 November 2026 on November-2026 data. Further information The updated Classification of Accounts Guide is available on the Bank of England’s statistical reporting webpage . Any queries concerning this notice should be directed to the Money and Credit Group by emailing DSDMCG@bankofengland.co.uk . Footnote A summary of all Statistical Notice items that are yet to come into effect are also available to view on the Statistical notices page . Statistical Notices should be received by all those responsible for the completion of Bank of England returns. To amend the circulation list please subscribe .
