title: Department of Homeland Security v. League of Women Voters
Treasury Identifies Nearly $15 Billion in Potential Iranian Shadow Banking
body: November 23, 2026 WASHINGTON —In a new Financial Trend Analysis , the U.S. Department of the Treasury’s Financial Crimes Enforcement Network (FinCEN) identified approximately $14.7 billion of financial activity from January 2025 to August 2026 potentially linked to Iranian shadow banking. As part of their compliance requirements, U.S. financial institutions flag suspicious activity to FinCEN, making it available to law enforcement and national security agencies. “Financial institutions are often the first line of defense in denying Iranian regime-linked funds access to the U.S. economy,” said Secretary of the Treasury Scott Bessent . “Treasury will continue to sever the financial lifelines on which the regime relies to fund its military, weapons programs, and terror proxies.” The trends and methods associated with potential Iranian shadow banking remained relatively consistent through 2026. Potential Iranian shadow banking networks continue to be connected across continents, most prominently in the United Arab Emirates (UAE), Hong Kong, and Singapore, and by the oil, shipping, investment, technology procurement, and other industries. Key Findings The most common routes for funds flagged by financial institutions were: from mainland China-based banks to UAE-based banks: approximately $2.6 billion; Singapore-based banks to UAE-based banks: approximately $981 million; and United Kingdom-based banks to UAE-based banks: approximately $922 million. The potential exploitation of companies registered in the Marshall Islands and British Virgin Islands, usually at addresses linked to corporate registries, emerged as an area of concern. Potential Iran-linked companies were involved in a diverse array of businesses, including shipping, trading, and oil. Reporting Suspicious Iran-Related Activity To support financial institutions in their Bank Secrecy Act reporting, FinCEN has previously issued several publications that highlight red flags on Iran-linked actors: FinCEN Advisory on the Iranian Regime’s Illicit Oil Smuggling Activities, Shadow Banking Networks, and Weapons Procurement Efforts (June 2025) FinCEN Alert on the Use of Front Companies, Financial Facilitators, and Digital Asset Infrastructure by Iran’s Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps to Evade Sanctions and Launder Proceeds (May 2026) FinCEN Alert to Counter Iranian Procurement Efforts for its Commercial Aviation Industry (September 2026) FinCEN Alert to Counter Iranian Abuse of Religious Charity Networks (October 2026) Through its whistleblower incentive program , FinCEN welcomes tips on Iran-related illicit finance . Individuals located in the United States or abroad who provide information about sanctions violations may be eligible for an award if the information they provide leads to a successful enforcement action that results in monetary penalties exceeding $1,000,000. As highlighted in FinCEN’s recent Bulletin ( available in several languages ), this includes information about violations of the Bank Secrecy Act or Office of Foreign Assets Control-administered sanctions programs that may involve the use of Iranian proxies and facilitators operating outside of Iran. ###

title: Operation Economic Outcast Disrupts Iran’s Global Shadow Banking Networks
body: November 23, 2026 WASHINGTON —Today, as part of Operation Economic Outcast, the U.S. Department of the Treasury sanctioned over two dozen Iranian exchange houses, front companies, and key personnel in a sweeping effort to disrupt Iran’s global shadow banking networks. As Iran’s economy remains battered by punishing economic sanctions and its oil revenues continue to decline, the regime’s shadow banking facilitators have increasingly failed to repatriate dwindling export earnings while simultaneously enriching themselves by stealing state resources that rightfully belong to the Iranian people. “Iran’s economy is underwater, and its leaders are panicking,” said Secretary of the Treasury Scott Bessent . “Iran’s shadow banking system is the last financial lifeline of a bankrupt regime. Treasury will continue dismantling these illicit networks until we have buried the head of the snake.” Today’s action targets the financial infrastructure that underpins much of Iran’s remaining foreign trade, disrupting the exchange houses, front companies, and facilitators that move billions of dollars through the international financial system to provide the regime access to foreign currency despite comprehensive sanctions. This action is being taken pursuant to the following Executive Orders (E.O.): E.O. 13902, which targets certain sectors of the Iranian economy, including Iran’s financial sector; E.O. 13224, as amended, a counter-terrorism designation authority; and E.O. 13871, which targets persons operating in various sectors of Iran’s metals industry. OPERATION ECONOMIC OUTCAST IS ISOLATING THE IRANIAN REGIME Announced by Secretary Bessent on August 24, 2026, dubbed Economic D-Day, Operation Economic Outcast is severing the remaining economic lifelines that sustain the Iranian regime. Treasury has mapped the networks, facilitators, and financial channels that Iran uses to smuggle oil, evade sanctions, and fund terror. Working with partners across the U.S. government, the European Union, United Kingdom, Gulf partners, and others, Treasury is targeting any source of the regime’s illicit revenue, as well as its sanctions evasion schemes to move funds. Operation Economic Outcast significantly expanded sanctions risk for those who continue to choose to do business with Iran.  Treasury warned that any entity facilitating money laundering or sanctions evasion on behalf of Iran risks being cut off from the U.S. financial system. It also expanded secondary sanctions exposure for those who continue doing business with the Iranian regime and will accelerate the pace of U.S. enforcement. More information on Operation Economic Outcast is available here . EXCHANGE HOUSES AND RAHBAR COMPANIES Iran’s shadow banking system is overseen by the Central Bank of Iran and relies on dozens of Iran-based exchange houses and “rahbar companies,” bank affiliates that manage sanctions evasion networks for their Iran-based clients. Exchange houses and rahbar companies work hand-in-hand to facilitate the financial underpinnings of Iran’s international trade through thousands of front companies in multiple jurisdictions, most prominently, but not exclusively, in Dubai and Hong Kong. Billions of dollars move through the international financial system in this fashion, sustaining the last remnants of Iran’s foreign trade. Iran-based Rahbar Bazargani Nesim Baharan Qeshm Company (Nesim Baharan) operates as the rahbar company for Bank Sarmayeh and works closely with Iranian exchange houses and their front companies to facilitate transactions on behalf of Bank Sarmayeh’s Iranian clients, which include major Iranian petrochemical companies. Sayyed Mohammad Jalali , Valiollah Hemmati , and Ali Kalhor act as senior officials of Nesim Baharan. Rahbar Bazargani Nesim Baharan Qeshm Company is being designated pursuant to E.O. 13902 for operating in the financial sector of the Iranian economy. Sayyed Mohammad Jalali, Valiollah Hemmati, and Ali Kalhor are being designated pursuant to E.O. 13902 for having acted or purported to act for or on behalf of, directly or indirectly, Rahbar Bazargani Nesim Baharan Qeshm Company. Iran-based Mina Fashki and Partners Exchange Company (Fashki Exchange) and Mellat Exchange Company are exchange houses operating within Iran’s shadow banking system. Mina Fashki and Farzad Fashki own and operate Fashki Exchange, while Mahmoud Akhlaghi , Parviz Fazlju , and Mohammad Hossein Abbasi are officials of Mellat Exchange Company. Note : This graphic updates an April 2026 version to include Bank Sarmayeh and its rahbar. Fashki Exchange and Mellat Exchange Company are being designated pursuant to E.O. 13902 for operating in the financial sector of the Iranian economy. Mina Fashki and Farzad Fashki are being designated pursuant to E.O. 13902 for having acted or purported to act for or on behalf of, directly or indirectly, Fashki Exchange. Mahmoud Akhlaghi, Parviz Fazlju, and Mohammad Hossein Abbasi are being designated pursuant to E.O. 13902 for having acted or purported to act for or on behalf of, directly or indirectly, Mellat Exchange Company. Dubai-based Grand Target Heavy Equipment and Machinery Spare Parts Trading L.L.C , Recaz Star General Trading LLC , Meethale Raw Materials Trading Company LLC , Hemraj Trading L.L.C , Ewan Al Madeena General Trading LLC , OGA Global General Trading L.L.C , Dexterous Global DMCC , Khore Al Hilal Goods Wholesalers Trading LLC , Türkiye-based Bogazici Gumrukleme Ithalat Ihracat Turizm Petrol Urunleri Sanayi Ve Ticaret Limited Sirketi , and Hong Kong-based Grandez Trading Limited are exchange house front companies used by Iran’s rahbar network to facilitate thousands of cross-border payments, worth billions of dollars, on behalf of Iranian clients. These front companies have enabled Iran to carry out thousands of financial transactions through the rahbar network. Khore Al Hilal Goods Wholesalers Trading LLC has been used extensively by U.S.-sanctioned Iranian exchange houses Opal Exchange, also known as Pedram Pirouzan Exchange , and Omid Sepah Exchange to move millions of dollars for Iranian Bank Sepah. Grandez Trading Limited is a front company used by the U.S.-sanctioned Iranian exchange house Mohsen Khandan and Partners Exchange . Recaz Star General Trading LLC has sent and received hundreds of payments totaling over $170 million from persons associated with Sadaf Exchange . OGA Global General Trading LLC has overseen millions of dollars’ worth of payments for the National Iranian Tanker Company , which operates Iran’s fleet of state-owned oil tankers. Grand Target Heavy Equipment and Machinery Spare Parts Trading L.L.C, Recaz Star General Trading LLC, Meethale Raw Materials Trading Company LLC, Hemraj Trading L.L.C, Ewan Al Madeena General Trading LLC, OGA Global General Trading L.L.C, Dexterous Global DMCC, Khore Al Hilal Goods Wholesalers Trading LLC, Bogazici Gumrukleme Ithalat Ihracat Turizm Petrol Urunleri Sanayi Ve Ticaret Limited Sirketi, and Grandez Trading Limited are being designated pursuant to E.O. 13902 for operating in the financial sector of the Iranian economy. SHADOW BANKING FRONT COMPANIES Iranian exchange houses and rahbar companies operate through a multi-jurisdictional web of layered front and shell companies that enable them to remit and receive payments overseas on behalf of their Iranian customers. Iranian companies that participate in the global economy, in some way or fashion, engage with the Iranian shadow banking system to facilitate imports and exports. For example, Dubai-based Robust Trading LLC has facilitated payments for the sanctioned Iran-based copper mining giant National Iranian Copper Industries Company . Similarly, HMS Trading FZE , the Dubai-based oil export and commercial front company of Iranian Shahr Bank, has used Dubai-based Integral Petro Energy Trading LLC to facilitate millions of dollars’ worth of liquefied petroleum gas sales by Iranian petrochemical exporter Kharg Petrochemical Company Limited. Robust Trading LLC is being designated pursuant to E.O. 13871 for having materially assisted, sponsored, or provided financial, material, or technological support for, or goods or services in support of, the National Iranian Copper Industries Company. Integral Petro Energy Trading LLC is being designated pursuant to E.O. 13902 for having materially assisted, sponsored, or provided financial, material, or technological support for, or goods or services to or in support of, HMS Trading FZE. Other Dubai-based front companies include Royah Altahabia Trading L.L.C , Alam Al Sahra Building Materials Trading Co. L.L.C , Berkeley Trading LLC , and Nordic International Trading LLC , which have been counterparties to millions of dollars’ worth of transactions involving Iranian financial broker front companies operating within Iran’s rahbar system. Since at least 2022, Berkeley Trading L.L.C has facilitated millions of dollars’ worth of transactions for clients of Iran-based Amin Exchange. Royah Altahabia Trading L.L.C, Alam Al Sahra Building Materials Trading Co. L.L.C, Berkeley Trading LLC, and Nordic International Trading LLC are being designated pursuant to E.O. 13902 for operating in the financial sector of the Iranian economy. Dubai-based Gespl International General Trading LLC has been used by the National Iranian Oil Company as part of its oil and petrochemicals sales mechanism and is actively involved in money laundering via Iran’s shadow banking mechanism. Gespl International General Trading LLC is being designated pursuant to E.O. 13902 for operating in the petrochemical sector of the Iranian economy. Iran’s military organs also utilize the shadow banking system. Iranian Armed Forces General Staff-associated Sepehr Energy Jahan Nama Pars Company (SEJ) and sanctioned shipping company Dragon Road Ltd utilized Dubai-based H N B Trading Co LLC to complete payment for the charter of the SERENE I (IMO 9197832); H N B Trading Co LLC received hundreds of thousands of dollars from a SEJ front company as part of this scheme. H N B Trading Co LLC is being designated pursuant to E.O. 13224, as amended, for having materially assisted, sponsored, or provided financial, material, or technological support for, or goods or services to or in support of, Sepehr Energy Jahan Nama Pars Company. IRAN CENTER FOR EXCHANGE Additionally, as part of today’s action, OFAC is taking action against the Iran-based Iran Center for Exchange of Currency and Gold (Iran Center for Exchange), which plays an essential intermediary role within Iran’s system of international trade. The Iran Center for Exchange provides the financial plumbing to match exporters, who earn foreign currency from sales abroad, to importers, who need foreign currency to purchase goods, for tens of billions of dollars’ worth of trade every year. While Iran’s shadow banking system moves the funds generated by Iran’s international trade, the Iran Center for Exchange plays matchmaker and guides these funds to their ultimate destination inside Iran. The Central Bank of Iran also utilizes bonds issued by the Iran Center for Exchange to help facilitate international trade using Russian roubles and Chinese yuan without reliance on the U.S. dollar. title: November 23, 2026 - FDA Approves First Treatment for Limb-Girdle Muscular Dystrophy Type 2I/R9
body: FDA News Release FDA Approves First Treatment for Limb-Girdle Muscular Dystrophy Type 2I/R9 For Immediate Release: November 23, 2026 The U.S. Food and Drug Administration today approved Welgemda (ribitol), the first medicine for treating limb-girdle muscular dystrophy type 2I/R9 (LGMD2I/R9), a rare inherited muscle disease, for adults and pediatric patients weighing at least 30 kg. Welgemda is the first therapy approved for any form of limb-girdle muscular dystrophy. “Today’s approval is a historic milestone for patients and families living with limb-girdle muscular dystrophy, delivering the first-ever FDA-approved treatment for this disease, backed by clinical evidence,” said Acting FDA Commissioner Kyle Diamantas, J.D. “Under the Trump Administration’s commitment to accelerating innovation and removing unnecessary barriers for rare disease therapies, while maintaining high standards for safety, the FDA is proud to deliver real hope and meaningful progress for patients who have waited far too long for options.” LGMD2I/R9 is caused by mutations in the FKRP gene, which disrupt a key biological process in muscle cells. In healthy individuals, the FKRP enzyme helps attach sugar molecules to a protein called alpha-dystroglycan, which acts as an anchor, helping muscle cells connect to surrounding tissue. When this process is disrupted, muscle cells become fragile and break down over time, leading to progressive weakness, difficulty walking, and in many patients, impaired breathing. Symptoms typically appear in childhood or early adulthood and worsen over time. “Limb-girdle muscular dystrophy is a progressive muscle disease that gradually takes away a patient’s ability to walk, breathe, and live independently, often beginning in childhood,” said Laura Jawidzik, M.D., Director of the Division of Neurology 2 in the FDA’s Center for Drug Evaluation and Research . “The clinical data supporting Welgemda's approval show meaningful improvements in walking speed and lung function, and we are encouraged by what that can mean for patients' daily lives.” The precise mechanism of Welgemda in the treatment of LGMD2I/R9 is not fully known, but may involve increases in a natural sugar molecule (matriglycan) that anchors alpha-dystroglycan in muscle tissue. The medicine is taken as an oral solution twice daily, mixed with water. Welgemda was evaluated in a randomized, placebo-controlled, double-blind study ( NCT05775848 ) involving 112 patients with genetically confirmed LGMD2I/R9. Patients were randomly assigned to receive either Welgemda or placebo for up to 36 months. At a planned interim analysis after 12 months of treatment, patients receiving Welgemda showed significant improvements in two key measures compared to those receiving placebo. Specifically, patients showed improvements in walking speed, measured by the 100-meter timed test, and lung function, measured by forced vital capacity (an indicator of respiratory muscle health). Patients treated with Welgemda also showed significant increases in glycosylated alpha-dystroglycan, indicating the drug was reaching its intended target at the proposed dose. The most common adverse reactions were gastrointestinal effects (e.g., diarrhea, stomach pain) and joint pain. Welgemda received Orphan Drug , Fast Track , and rare pediatric disease designations for the treatment of LGMD2I/R9. Welgemda is manufactured by ML Bio Solutions Inc. and distributed by BridgeBio Pharma, Inc. title: November 23, 2026 - FDA Approves First New Hormone Therapy for Early-Stage Breast Cancer in More Than 20 Years
body: FDA News Release FDA Approves First New Hormone Therapy for Early-Stage Breast Cancer in More Than 20 Years For Immediate Release: November 23, 2026 The U.S. Food and Drug Administration today approved Wilserdly (giredestrant), used alone after surgery in adults with estrogen receptor–positive, HER2-negative breast cancer — the most common subtype of the disease. A once-daily oral tablet, Wilserdly is the first new hormone therapy for early-stage breast cancer in more than 20 years. Wilserdly belongs to a class of medicines called oral estrogen receptor antagonists. In estrogen receptor–positive breast cancer, estrogen binds to receptors (proteins) on cancer cells and signals them to grow. Estrogen receptor antagonists like Wilserdly block this process and break down the receptors, cutting off a key driver of tumor growth. “Like many Americans, I have seen breast cancer affect my own family. That experience makes the work we do at FDA deeply personal,” said Acting FDA Commissioner Kyle Diamantas, J.D. “Even as we recognize how far treatment has come for early-stage breast cancer, the Trump administration knows that patients and their families are counting on us to keep building on that progress, and that’s what we’ve done with today’s approval.” The approval covers adults with estrogen receptor–positive, HER2-negative, stage I, II, or III disease with an intermediate to high risk of recurrence following surgery. Breast cancer is the second most common cancer among women in the United States. An estimated 321,910 new cases are expected in women and 2,670 in men in 2026, approximately 70% of which are estrogen receptor–positive and HER2-negative. “For patients with early-stage hormone-driven breast cancer, the goal after surgery is to keep the cancer from coming back,” said Angelo de Claro, M.D., director of the FDA’s Oncology Center of Excellence . “Our review focused on whether Wilserdly could reduce that risk more effectively than the hormone therapies patients already receive. The evidence showed that it could, supporting today’s approval of a new option for patients at intermediate to high risk of recurrence.” In the randomized, multicenter lidERA Breast Cancer trial ( NCT04961996 ), 4,170 adults with this subtype at intermediate to high risk of recurrence were assigned to receive Wilserdly or standard of care hormone therapy — tamoxifen or an aromatase inhibitor (anastrozole, letrozole, or exemestane) for up to 5 years. Wilserdly reduced the risk of invasive breast cancer recurrence or death by 30% compared with standard hormone therapy (140 versus 196 patients experienced an event during follow-up). This made lidERA the first phase III trial to demonstrate a benefit with an oral estrogen receptor antagonist in early-stage breast cancer. At 3 years, 92.4% of patients taking Wilserdly were alive and free of invasive breast cancer, compared with 89.6% of those taking standard hormone therapy. This translates to about 28 more patients out of every 1,000 alive and free of invasive breast cancer at 3 years. Patients receiving Wilserdly also had a lower risk of cancer returning in another part of the body. Patients are being followed to determine whether Wilserdly helps them live longer. The applicant has agreed to submit these results to the FDA as a postmarketing commitment . The FDA previously approved Wilserdly on November 16, 2026, in combination with everolimus for certain adults with estrogen receptor–positive, HER2-negative, ESR1-mutated advanced or metastatic breast cancer whose disease recurred or progressed during or after prior endocrine therapy. That approval was based on the evERA Breast Cancer trial ( NCT05306340 ). The most common side effects (≥10%) of Wilserdly are muscle and joint pain, hot flashes, tiredness, headache, nausea, slower-than-normal heart rate, dizziness, numbness or tingling in the hands and feet. Common blood test changes include increased liver enzymes, lower blood counts, high blood fat levels, and changes in mineral levels and kidney test results. Wilserdly may harm a developing baby if taken during pregnancy. Women who have not completed menopause should also receive an additional hormone-suppressing medicine with Wilserdly. Men may also receive this medicine, as determined by their healthcare provider. The FDA’s evaluation of the application was supported by an Assessment Aid voluntarily submitted by the applicant. The FDA granted Priority Review to the application. The approval was granted to Genentech, Inc, a member of the Roche Group. title: Operation Economic Outcast Targets Corrupt Regime Insiders Exploiting Iran’s Oil Sector for Personal Gain
body: November 20, 2026 WASHINGTON —Today, as part of Operation Economic Outcast, the U.S. Department of the Treasury is targeting key “oil trustees” the Iranian regime relies on to facilitate the sale of oil abroad. With no oil on the water outside of the U.S. military blockade and no oil loaded onto vessels since the start of Operation Economic Outcast, the regime is attempting to recoup billions of dollars from its oil trustees.  In many cases, these corrupt trustees have kept the oil revenue for personal gain. “Iran’s tyrannical regime never fails to put its own interests before those of its own citizens, even as ordinary Iranians face shortages of bread and fuel,” said Secretary of the Treasury Scott Bessent .  “The regime has exhausted its seaborne oil supply, and it may never see the revenue from the oil it has already sold. The ship is sinking.” The designations imposed today are being taken pursuant to Executive Order (E.O.) 13902, which targets the Iranian petroleum, petrochemical, and aviation sectors, among other key sectors of the Iranian economy, and E.O. 13224, as amended, a counterterrorism authority. OPERATION ECONOMIC OUTCAST IS ISOLATING THE IRANIAN REGIME Announced by Secretary Bessent on August 24, 2026, dubbed Economic D-Day , Operation Economic Outcast is severing the remaining economic lifelines that sustain the Iranian regime.  Treasury has mapped the networks, facilitators, and financial channels that Iran uses to smuggle oil, evade sanctions, and fund terror.  Working with partners across the U.S. government, the European Union, United Kingdom, Gulf partners, and others, Treasury is targeting any source of the regime’s illicit revenue, as well as its sanctions evasion schemes to move funds. Operation Economic Outcast has significantly expanded sanctions risk for those who continue to choose to do business with Iran.  Treasury warned that any entity facilitating money laundering or sanctions evasion on behalf of Iran risks being cut off from the U.S. financial system. Operation Economic Outcast has also expanded sanctions exposure for non-U.S. persons who continue doing business with the Iranian regime and will accelerate the pace of U.S. enforcement. More information on Operation Economic Outcast is available here . UNTRUSTWORTHY TRUSTEES Mohammad Javad Bavand (Bavand) and Majid Taj (Taj), the brother of the Iranian Football Federation’s president, operate as part of a network of regime insiders tasked with obtaining desperately needed cash by selling from Iran’s dwindling oil reserves.  Bavand, a former IRGC intelligence officer, has spearheaded this effort, entrusting a group of personal contacts, including Taj, to recoup Iran’s oil funds located in third countries.  The Iranian regime continues to entrust Bavand and Taj’s network with facilitating Iran’s oil sales, despite members owing billions of dollars to the regime from previous sales.  Bavand has worked with a variety of illicit oil trading actors, including the IRGC and Sepehr Energy Jahan Nama Pars Company (SEJ), a U.S.-designated front company tasked with selling oil for the Iranian Armed Forces General Staff. Mohammad Javad Bavand and Majid Taj are being designated pursuant to E.O. 13902 for operating in the petroleum sector of the Iranian economy. REGIME FACILITATORS Mohammadhossein Servati (Servati), the son of IRGC Brigadier General Mohsen Servati, has held executive positions at companies operated by SEJ, including SEJ front company Xin Rui Jin Trad Co., Limited , and Sepehr Energy Hamta Pars , a subsidiary of SEJ.  Xin Rui Jin Trad Co., Limited brokered and received shipments of Iranian oil on behalf of SEJ for delivery to Chinese teapot refineries. Mohammadhossein Servati is being designated pursuant to E.O. 13224, as amended, for having materially assisted, sponsored, or provided financial, material, or technological support for, or goods or services to or in support of, Sepehr Energy Jahan Nama Pars Company. Mojtaba Arabnejad (Mojtaba) is the son of the designated Iranian businessman and CEO of Iran’s Mahan Air , Hamid Arabnejad .  Using his familial ties and special connections with the Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps-Qods Force (IRGC-QF), Mojtaba has been involved in purchasing aircraft parts for Mahan Air and procuring weapons for the Iranian military under the auspices of agricultural companies.  Like others designated today, Mojtaba has overseen oil sales for the Iranian regime, the proceeds from which have supported Mahan Air. Mojtaba Arabnejad is being designated pursuant to E.O. 13224, as amended, for having materially assisted, sponsored, or provided financial, material, or technological support for, or goods or services to or in support of, Mahan Air.
